theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Health Care (+2.87%) and Consumer Staples (+1.46%) led the market today, while Technology (-2.80%) and Industrials (-0.61%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.49% versus +1.62% for defensives and +0.62% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +0.84% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.49%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up +0.60%, outperforming large caps. The VIX fell 0.94% to 26.36, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold slipped 2.25% to $3,549.10, crude oil was little changed at $80.78, and bitcoin slipped 0.82% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
